area: The pre-M2 code (NEXT.md "Next, before M2", the rulings of 2026-09-25) and the pre-M2 pass (NEXT.md "In flight")
summary: All five items NEXT.md:23-25 lists are already in the code. The pass built them before #704 merged into this branch (93586e7), so that bullet is stale, and so is V3_PARITY.md §5 item 1, which points at it. Evidence: Provenance.Drift (kernel/Provenance.cs:61, commit b070e5e); AggregateQuery.Of internal, with a synonym check before every Measure (io/SqlServer.cs:241-244 and :349-356, commit 98ff3c4); a host required for each environment and compared by R15 for every environment (io/Environments.cs:86-89, io/LocalServer.cs:254-273); check drift built once per commit, the database read once by Extract, the plan run package to package (io/Ssdt.cs:249-251, io/DriftCheck.cs:54-78, commit 6da60be); and the Extended Events test running a matching check drift, a drifted one and read --from env:dev (tests/Io.Tests/DriftTests.cs:282). The pre-M2 pass is finished: five adapter merges (d1e2d95, abd6afc, 627759e, 377240b, 5a5aa6b), then the names commits once the operator had answered round two (review page database, 2026-09-26 01:31-01:51 UTC), then the tests refactor (06fd171..b35bc24), then the other model's review applied (7aa30ca..81beef2: S1-S30, N3-N16 and M1-M3 'of the pre-M2 review'). Three things remain. One is code: round-two finding DF-5, which the operator marked fix, has no commit (no system dacpacs in the tool folder). One is a small test gap: no test drives the absent "host" key. The rest is documents: NEXT.md, V3_PARITY.md §0 and §5 and rows PAR-002 and PAR-012, and V3_MILESTONES.md §7 still describe the pass as pending. The laptop check still names a tool folder built at e0a4db94, before the pass. The two later lines dated 2026-09-25 say "from M2", so they belong to M2, but no M2 work package row carries them yet.

items.name: The two 'from M2' rulings: check drift lists, as notes, the objects the database holds that the tag lacks (DECISIONS.md:59), and check drift's --at takes dacpac:<the artifact Octopus deployed> (DECISIONS.md:60)
items.evidence: Both lines begin 'from M2', so by the plan's words they belong to M2 itself, not to the pre-M2 pass. No V3_MILESTONES.md §8 row carries them (WP 2.1-2.6 at :518-525); WP 1.7 (:472) built check drift. Today cli/Check.cs:48-50 reads --at through GitRef.Of only, with 'ref:' optional. DriftCheck.Request.At is a GitRef (io/DriftCheck.cs:20). Run always builds (:54). The check schema's 'commit' requires 40-64 hex (cli/Check.cs:25). The kernel already parses dacpac:<path> as Target.Dacpac (kernel/Target.cs:31, :66).
items.remaining: When M2 opens, write both into a WP row with a decision line. WP 2.5 (lane B, io/Predict and the verbs) is the natural home, because io/DriftCheck.cs and cli/Check.cs are its verb surface. Then: (a) --at accepts ref:<ref>, a bare ref or dacpac:<path>. Request.At becomes a closed source (the kernel's Target.GitRef or Target.Dacpac). For a dacpac, Run skips Ssdt.Build and opens the file with Ssdt.Open. Answer.Commit becomes nullable, the check schema's commit becomes nullable, and the package's fingerprint is added. Regenerate cli/schemas/dbchange.check.1.schema.json. (b) A second, report-only DacFx.Plan of the same package against the same extract, with DropObjectsNotInSource=true. Make it a plan option on DacFx.Plan, not a PublishProfile, so Strict stays the profile as loaded and nothing can publish under it (S1). Each drop operation that the first plan does not hold becomes a Finding.Note (code e.g. drift.not-in-tag, its text held to the register). Neither changes the outcome or the exit.

risks: NEXT.md, V3_PARITY.md §5 item 1 and §0 send the next wave to build code that already exists. A worker that takes them literally will duplicate or churn Provenance, AggregateQuery, Environments, Ssdt.Build or DriftTests. The real pre-M2 code remainder is DF-5 plus one test.

The round-two review page's gate card records option 0, 'After this round's rulings and one pre-M2 pass, start M2' (2026-09-26 01:51 UTC). This run's request says M2 waits on the operator's go, and that instruction takes precedence. Do not read the card as the go.

The laptop check (M1 exit 1, S1, S3) names a tool folder built at e0a4db94. That folder predates the pass: the old LoadFromDatabase-plus-live-Script route, the 'estate' names, and posture.json without 'host'. A report from it would measure code the branch no longer runs. Its posture file would also be refused at head (environments.host).

Provenance's properties are { get; init; } (kernel/Provenance.cs:34-52). Any assembly can therefore write `drift with { Change = x, Schema = y }` and bypass the per-kind constructors the ruling asks for, or give a drift claim ExistingData, which 'reads no data'. Making them get-only closes that. It costs ProvenanceTests.cs:37 and :41, which use `with`; the 'nothing lacking' case would wait for WP 2.1's prediction constructor. WP 2.1 also needs Fingerprint.Of(Change), which does not exist: kernel/Fingerprint.cs has Of(bytes), Of(string), Of(SortedArray<Element>) and Of(DeployReport) at :27, :34, :43 and :85.

DF-5 adds two NuGet packages that the cache lacks (restore from api.nuget.org) and changes the published tool folder. Both CI operating systems and ToolFolderTests must see the new Extensions/ tree. The folder layout under Extensions/Microsoft/SQLDB/Extensions/SqlServer/160/SqlSchemas/ follows SSDT's convention and should be confirmed by the new build test before it is relied on.

Eleven items of the other model's pre-M2 review (S3, S7, S8, S15, S17, S22, S29, N1, N2, N10, N15) are cited by no commit, and that review is not available to check. They may be no-change verdicts or open defects.
The operator's notes on the review page (decision 2.5 returned with a question; plan-STATUS marked discuss) have no reply in the repository or on the page.

io/SqlServer.cs (997 lines) and io/Ssdt.cs (767) are above the 500-line-per-code-file budget that task #7 is enforcing. The from-M2 drift work touches io/DriftCheck.cs and io/DacFx.cs beside them and would collide with that split if both run in one wave.
